item.title: Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art: Tadao Ando on the Waterfront — Guide
item.description: The Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art is the largest art museum in western Japan and as much an architectural destination as an art one: its building, completed in 2002 by Tadao Ando, is a monumental composition of raw concrete, glass volumes and open external stairways stepping down to the Kobe waterfront, built as part of the city’s cultural recovery after the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake. The collection spans modern Japanese and Western sculpture, prints and painting, and even without a ticket the terraces, stairways and sea-facing spaces are free to explore.
